description:
Run Python that calls Hermes tools programmatically. Use when you need 3+ tool calls with logic between them: filtering/reducing large outputs before they enter context, branching, or loops (N pages/files, retry on failure). Use normal tool calls for single calls, results you must reason over in full, or anything needing user interaction.

Calls run in a persistent session kernel: variables, imports, and loaded data survive across execute_code calls while the session kernel remains cached. Local session kernels may be evicted when the local process reaches its max_session_kernels limit; local eviction sets kernel.state_reset=true and explains that variables must be recreated. Remote-backed kernels share that cap but their cap eviction is not reported; a remote kernel that died or disconnected sets kernel.state_lost=true. Check kernel.reused=false before relying on earlier variables. A timed-out or interrupted call loses that state.

Available via `from hermes_tools import ...`:

  web_search(query: str, limit: int = 5) -> dict
    Returns {"data": {"web": [{"url", "title", "description"}, ...]}}
  web_extract(urls: list[str], char_limit: int = None) -> dict
    Returns {"results": [{"url", "title", "content", "error"}, ...]} where content is markdown.
    No LLM summarization. Pages over char_limit (default 15000) are head+tail truncated; full text stored on disk (path in the content footer).
  read_file(path: str, offset: int = 1, limit: int = 2000, node: str = None) -> dict
    Lines are 1-indexed. Returns {"content": "...", "total_lines": N}; errors raise HermesToolError.
  write_file(path: str, content: str, node: str = None) -> dict
    Always overwrites the entire file; an existing file must be read_file'd first or the write is refused. Errors raise HermesToolError.
  search_files(pattern: str, target="content", path=".", file_glob=None, limit=50, order="discovery", node: str = None) -> dict
    target: "content" (search inside files) or "files" (find files by name). Returns {"matches": [...]}; errors raise HermesToolError.
  patch(path: str, old_string: str, new_string: str, replace_all: bool = False, node: str = None) -> dict
    Replaces old_string with new_string in the file; errors raise HermesToolError.
  terminal(command: str, timeout=None, workdir=None, node: str = None) -> dict
    Foreground only (no background/pty). Returns {"output": "...", "exit_code": N}

Limits: 5-minute timeout, max 50 tool calls per call. Stdout over 50KB shows head/tail inline; the FULL text is auto-saved to a file whose path rides in the result.

Scripts run in the session's working directory. Interpreter: the project's activated venv/conda python when one is active (VIRTUAL_ENV/CONDA_PREFIX — matches terminal()); otherwise Hermes's own python (the common case — stdlib plus Hermes's deps; check `import x` before relying on project packages).

Tool calls return parsed dicts on success. The file tools `read_file`, `write_file`, `patch`, and `search_files` raise `HermesToolError` when their result contains an error; other tools keep returning their error dicts so scripts can inspect fields such as `exit_code` or `success`. Helpers require imports: `from hermes_tools import json_parse, shell_quote, retry`. json_parse(text) — tolerant json.loads for terminal() output; shell_quote(s) — shlex.quote for dynamic shell args; retry(fn, max_attempts=3, delay=2) — exponential backoff.
name: execute_code

code.description: Python code to execute. Import tools with `from hermes_tools import web_search, terminal, ...` and print your final result to stdout.

reset.description: Discard the kernel's persistent state and start fresh before running this code.
